sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
பதறி வருவாள் பத்மலோசனி அன்பர்
கதறி நிற்கும் நிலை கண்டாலே
sections.translit:
padhaRi varuvAL padhmalOchani anbar
kadhaRi niRkum nilai kaNdAlE
sections.en: The lotus eyed Goddess Padhmalochani will come rushing when she hears her devotees cry in despair.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
சிதறி ஓட வைப்பாள் வினைகளை திருவாலி
நகரி நித்யகல்யாணி நிற்குண சுந்தரி
sections.translit:
sidhaRi Oda vaippAL vinaigaLai thiruvAli
nagari nithyakalyANi niRguNa sundhari
sections.en: The ever-auspicious, beautiful, and flawless goddess of Thiruvali city will drive away all your sins.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
அங்கம் யாவும் குளிர ஸ்ரீஹரியின்
பொங்கும் சினம் தணிய வழியறியாமல்
கோடி தேவரும் மனம் வருந்தியே
வாடி பாடிட பதியை நாடி ஓடி வந்தது போல்
sections.translit:
angam yAvum kuLira srIhariyin
pongum sinam thaNiya vazhiyaRiyAmal
kOdi dhEvarum manam varundhiyE
vAdi pAdida pathiyai nAdi Odi vandhadhu pOl
sections.en: There was a time when crores of celestial Gods did not know how to control the anger and cool the body of Sri Hari after his killing the demon, Hiranyakasipu. They chanted and prayed in utter distress to Goddess Lakshmi. She will rush to her devotees whenever they cry in despair, just like the time she ran looking for her husband, sat on his lap, embraced and calmed him.

notes: A ferocious Narasimhar (half-man, half-lion incarnation of Lord Vishnu) could not control his anger after killing the demon, Hiranyakasipu. Lord Siva and his creation, Prithyankara devi, both fought with Hari but to no avail. Siva took the form of Sarabeswara (half-bird, half-man form) in this fight but could not control Vishnu’s anger. All of the celestials then begged Goddess Lakshmi to find alternate ways to calm down Lord Vishnu. Mahalakshmi rushed to the spot and hugged her Lord and sat on his lap, and this finally cooled him off. Vishnu in this divya kshetram in Thiruvaali appears in an alinganam, or an embracing pose, with the Goddess sitting on his lap. For details, see: Thiruvali LakshmiNarasimhar Temple Legend Also see: Azagiyasinger Temple Sthalapuranam
